clues.text: This is a port town in Argentina, in the Rio Negro province. It sits by a wide gulf on the sea.
clues.narrowing: rules out all but the Rio Negro coast of Argentina

source.quote: San Antonio Oeste is a port city in the Argentine province of Río Negro, and head of the department of San Antonio.

clues.text: This sea town was too dry to live in at first. Its first homes failed for lack of fresh water, so folk moved west.
clues.narrowing: points to a dry coast where fresh water is scarce

source.quote: Water scarcity led the original settlement to fail in 1905, leading the community to settle west of the gulf, in what today is San Antonio Oeste.

clues.text: A team from Spain first found this gulf in seventeen seventy-nine. They set up a small post here on its shore.
clues.narrowing: adds a Spanish-era gulf post from 1779

source.quote: Discovered by an expedition of the Spanish Empire in 1779, San Matías Gulf became the site of an outpost, San Antonio (so named in honor of St. Anthony of Padua).

clues.text: This port once led the wool trade for all Patagonia. When wool prices fell, the port shut in nineteen forty-four.
clues.narrowing: narrows to the great wool ports of Patagonia

source.quote: It later became the site of Punta Verde, the leading port for the large wool export industry of Patagonia, though the collapse in the wool market during the 1930s and 1940s led to the port's closure in 1944.

clues.text: Close by lies a famed cove known for its caves. Trips to that cove now bring crowds to this port town.
clues.narrowing: confirms the port by its famed cave cove next door

source.quote: San Antonio Oeste benefited afterwards from a growth in tourism in nearby Las Grutas, a scenic cove known for its grottoes.

clues.text: This town is in north Argentina. It sits at the north tip of the Rio Negro province, near La Pampa.
clues.narrowing: rules out all but northern Rio Negro in Argentina

source.quote: Colonia Catriel, or simply Catriel, is a town in the northern tip of the province of Río Negro, Argentina, near the border with La Pampa Province.

clues.text: Summers here are hot and dry. Winters bring a dry, strong wind, and snow is rare in this dry land.
clues.narrowing: points to a dry band with hot summers and rare snow

source.quote: The town has a dry and temperate climate, with hot summers and winters which barely see snow. A characteristic dry strong wind is also common.

clues.text: Oil came here in nineteen fifty-nine. The state oil firm set up wells nearby, and the town grew fast.
clues.narrowing: adds the oil boom that began in 1959

source.quote: The main economic activity in and around the town is oil extraction, which started in 1959 and made the city grow fast, as state owned YPF set extraction points nearby.

clues.text: This town took its name from a chief. Tales say he stood up for the state in fights with other native groups.
clues.narrowing: links the town name to a native chief in old tales

source.quote: Catriel was named after Cacique Catriel, a Native American who according to several stories participated in the defence of Argentine government interests against aborigines.

clues.text: Today one oil giant runs most of the work here. Petrobras has put big funds into this town.
clues.narrowing: confirms the oil town led today by Petrobras

source.quote: However, nowadays the main oil company in the city is Petrobras, which has made several investments in the city.
